claim.quote: Our result, rp = 0.831 ± 0.007stat ± 0.012syst femtometres, is smaller than the most recent high-precision e–p measurement

name: PRad: proton charge radius from magnetic-spectrometer-free electron-proton scattering
notes: The PRad-II proposal and the target paper (arXiv:2103.01749) state that the PRad result agrees with the muonic-hydrogen value.

summary.plain: PRad measured how electrons scatter from protons at extremely small angles, without a magnetic spectrometer, and found the proton's charge radius to be 0.831 femtometres. That is smaller than the average of earlier electron-scattering results and bears on the 'proton radius puzzle'.
summary.technical: Elastic e-p cross section at Q^2 from 2.1 x 10^-4 to 6 x 10^-2 (GeV/c)^2 from 1.1 and 2.2 GeV beams on a windowless hydrogen gas target, normalised to simultaneous e-e (Moller) scattering: r_p = 0.831 +- 0.007 stat +- 0.012 syst fm, 2.7 standard deviations below the average of all e-p experimental results.

title: A small proton charge radius from an electron–proton scattering experiment
why_it_matters: An independent, low-systematics electron-scattering determination of the proton radius, bearing on the discrepancy between muonic-hydrogen and earlier measurements.
